fullPassage:
[1번] Local elementary schools are invited to join us in celebrating the 25th anniversary of the city's subway system. We're asking elementary students to create a poster that will be displayed in our subways during the celebration. The theme of the poster should be "uniting communities." Be creative and show us what the subway means to you and your community. Each student may submit only one poster by September 22. This event is less about competition than it is about showcasing community spirit. However, the winner will receive a special subway tour, and the winner's school will receive $500. There will also be a promotional photoshoot featuring the winner and all of the winner's classmates. The judging period will take no longer than one week. So we expect to announce a winner by October 1. We hope everyone participates!

[2번] Have you ever walked through a city on a windy day? If you have, you probably noticed that the wind was stronger near tall buildings. This is called the "downdraught effect." Generally, the higher you go, the stronger the winds are. When strong winds high above the ground hit a tall building, they can't go through it. Instead, they go up, down, or around the sides of the building. The wind that shoots down to the ground is strong at street level. Having several tall buildings near one another can also increase wind speeds. This is due to the "channeling effect," which occurs when the wind blows through the narrow spaces between the buildings. It's similar to water flowing in a river — the narrower the space, the faster it moves.

[3번] Hoarding disorder is a mental illness characterized by the inability to get rid of possessions that have no use or value. It is often accompanied by "excessive acquisition," which means sufferers feel the need to own as many things as possible. Hoarding behavior tends to start at an early age and becomes more and more extreme as the person grows older. Once it becomes a significant problem, it is generally treated with behavioral therapy, which helps hoarders make better decisions about keeping or getting rid of their belongings. However, as hoarding disorder can be a complex condition with multiple causes, this treatment often takes a long time, and additional methods may be required.

[4번] Have you ever seen rows of identical fruit or vegetables in the supermarket? They may look pretty, but consider this — perfectly fine produce that looks a little different is being wasted. In fact, some farmers end up throwing away as much as 50 percent of their harvest because it doesn't look quite right. Fortunately, this is beginning to change. All of this wasted produce tastes just as good as what they sell in the supermarket. So there are now some organizations that buy ugly produce from farmers and sell it to consumers at prices as much as 30 percent lower than normal. Not only does this practice benefit farmers and consumers, but it also helps protect the environment, since farmers don't have to waste resources growing unwanted produce.

[5번] Palm scanning is a form of biometrics that uses the palm of a person's hand as a unique form of identification. More specifically, it maps the vein patterns that are found in the person's palm. After the scan is complete, it compares the patterns to existing scans to look for matches. If there are no matches, it is added to the database. Once recorded and stored, these palm scans can serve as a person's digital signature for both online and in-person transactions. As a result, people no longer need to carry credit cards or cash. Soon, people may be able to make purchases with just their hand. Furthermore, there is little chance of fraud. No biometric system is harder to fool than palm scans. Vein patterns are unique, and unlike fingerprints, cannot easily be taken without a person's knowledge. This guarantees a level of safety greater than that of any other system.

[6번] It is now believed that deserts may be perfect places for harvesting solar power. If this is true, there would be no other place as ideal as the Sahara, the world's largest desert. Unfortunately, solar farms in the desert could have adverse environmental effects. For example, covering half the Sahara with solar farms would raise local temperatures by approximately 2.5 °C. This warming would not be limited to the desert — it would spread around the globe, eventually increasing the world's average temperature by 0.39 °C. This could speed up global warming by melting sea ice and exposing the dark water beneath it, which absorbs greater amounts of solar energy than sea ice does. Rising temperatures in the Sahara could also cause other problems by changing global precipitation patterns, including droughts in the Amazon and more frequent tropical cyclones.

[7번] Research suggests that when we use the term "brilliant," we usually apply it to men rather than women. It is said that this is an unconscious bias that occurs all across the world. It may also be the reason why even brilliant women are less likely to be employed in fields where a high level of intelligence is prized, such as math and science. A study conducted in 2016 analyzed 14 million student reviews of university faculty members. It found that male professors were two to three times more likely to be described with the words "brilliant" or "genius" than female professors were. Furthermore, students were more likely to use these words in reference to professors of physics and philosophy, two fields with relatively few women. These results suggest that we either underestimate women or overestimate men. This is why we need to be aware of the words we use and think about why we use them.

[8번] Coral reefs are being threatened by unusually warm water that is causing them to bleach and die. One team of researchers has devised an unusual plan to deal with this. They intend to record the sounds of healthy reefs and then play them near reefs that are suffering from severe bleaching. A healthy reef is noisy, and it is believed that this attracts young fish, letting them know that this is a place where they can safely live. Damaged reefs, on the contrary, are silent. They attract few new inhabitants, which causes them to degrade even further. The researchers tested their idea at a reef severely affected by bleaching. Healthy reef sounds were played in certain locations for 40 days. At the end of this period, the researchers found that the areas where the sounds were played had attracted twice as many young fish as places that were left silent.

det.korean: announcing → announce (expect to 뒤 to부정사이므로 동사원형)

det.tip: expect to + 동사원형 → to announce. to announcing은 틀림

det.korean: the calmer the air becomes=공기가 더 잔잔해진다 / the warmer the day feels=날이 더 따뜻해진다 / the stronger the winds are=바람이 더 세진다 / the lower the clouds sit=구름이 더 낮게 깔린다

빈칸 문장은 'Generally, the higher you go, ___(일반적으로 높이 올라갈수록, ___)'예요. 「the+비교급 ~, the+비교급 ~」 구문으로, 높이 올라갈수록 무엇이 어떻게 되는지 생각해요. 뒤에 '센 바람이 건물을 친다'는 내용이 이어져요.

① the calmer the air becomes(공기가 잔잔해짐): 뒤 내용(센 바람)과 반대

② the warmer the day feels(따뜻해짐): 온도 이야기가 아님

③ the stronger the winds are(바람이 더 세짐): 높이 올라갈수록 바람이 더 세진다는 흐름과 일치 ←정답

④ the lower the clouds sit(구름이 낮게): 구름 이야기가 아님
det.tip: the higher you go, ___ → the stronger the winds are (높을수록 더 셈)

questions.passage: Hoarding disorder is a mental illness characterized by the inability to get rid of possessions that have no use or value. It is often accompanied by "excessive acquisition," which means sufferers feel the need to own as many things as possible. Hoarding behavior tends to start at an early age and becomes more and more extreme as the person grows older. Once it becomes a significant problem, it is generally treated with behavioral therapy, which helps hoarders make better decisions about keeping or getting rid of their belongings. However, as hoarding disorder can be a complex condition with multiple causes, this treatment often takes a long time, and additional methods may be required.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문 'a mental illness characterized by the inability to get rid of possessions that have no use or value' → 일치
det.analysis:
① 나이가 들수록 저절로 나아진다: 본문은 'becomes more and more extreme(점점 더 극심해진다)'이라 반대예요.

② 최소한으로만 유지하려 한다: 'own as many things as possible(가능한 한 많이 소유)'과 반대예요.

③ 원인이 하나로 명확해 치료가 빠르다: 'a complex condition with multiple causes ~ takes a long time(원인이 여럿이라 오래 걸림)'과 반대예요.

④ 쓸모없는 물건을 버리지 못하는 무능력과 관련된 정신 질환: 첫 문장 정의(the inability to get rid of possessions that have no use or value)와 일치해요. ←정답
det.tip: 핵심 정의: inability to get rid of useless possessions = 쓸모없는 물건을 못 버림

ch: 저장 강박은 나이가 들수록 저절로 나아진다.
저장 강박은 원인이 하나로 명확해 치료가 빠르다.
저장 강박은 쓸모없는 물건을 버리지 못하는 무능력과 관련된 정신 질환이다.

questions.passage: Have you ever seen rows of identical fruit or vegetables in the supermarket? They may look pretty, but consider this — perfectly fine produce that looks a little different is being ①<u>wasting</u>. In fact, some farmers end up throwing away as much as 50 percent of their harvest because it doesn't look quite right. Fortunately, this is beginning to change. All of this wasted produce ②<u>tastes</u> just as good as what they sell in the supermarket. So there are now some organizations that ③<u>buy</u> ugly produce from farmers and sell it to consumers at prices as much as 30 percent lower than normal. Not only does this practice benefit farmers and consumers, but it also helps protect the environment, since farmers don't have to waste resources ④<u>growing</u> unwanted produce.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: wasting → wasted (is being + 과거분사: 진행형 수동태)
det.analysis:
① wasting: 'perfectly fine produce ~ is being ___'에서 농산물은 '낭비되는' 대상이에요. 진행형 수동태는 'be동사 + being + 과거분사(p.p.)' 형태라, being 뒤에는 과거분사 wasted가 와야 해요. -ing형 wasting은 능동이라 틀림 ←정답

② tastes: 주어 'All of this wasted produce(농산물)'는 단수 취급이라 단수동사 tastes — 적절

③ buy: 'organizations that buy ~'에서 관계대명사 that의 선행사 organizations가 복수라 buy — 적절

④ growing: 'waste resources ___ unwanted produce' 자원을 낭비하며 재배하는 동시동작을 나타내는 분사 — 적절
det.tip: 진행형 수동태 = be + being + 과거분사 → is being wasted (wasting 아님)

questions.passage: Palm scanning is a form of biometrics that uses the palm of a person's hand as a unique form of identification. More specifically, it maps the vein patterns that are found in the person's palm. After the scan is complete, it compares the patterns to existing scans to look for matches. If there are no matches, it is added to the database. Once recorded and stored, these palm scans can serve as a person's digital signature for both online and in-person transactions. As a result, people no longer need to carry credit cards or cash. Soon, people may be able to make purchases with just their hand. Furthermore, there is little chance of fraud. No biometric system is harder to fool than palm scans. Vein patterns are unique, and unlike fingerprints, cannot easily be taken without a person's knowledge. <u>This</u> guarantees a level of safety greater than that of any other system.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 This가 가리키는 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: This = 앞 문장 'Vein patterns are unique ... cannot easily be taken without a person's knowledge', 즉 정맥 패턴이 고유하고 본인 모르게 채취될 수 없다는 점
det.analysis:
밑줄 문장은 'This guarantees a level of safety greater than that of any other system(이것이 다른 어떤 시스템보다 큰 안전을 보장한다)'이에요. 무엇이 안전을 보장하는지 바로 앞 문장을 봐야 해요. 앞 문장은 '정맥 패턴은 고유하고, 지문과 달리 본인 모르게 쉽게 채취될 수 없다'는 내용이에요.

❌ ① 카드·현금 대체 — 편리함에 관한 것으로, 안전을 보장하는 근거가 아니에요.

✅ ② 정맥 패턴이 고유하며 본인 모르게 채취될 수 없다는 점 — 바로 앞 문장 내용으로, 이것이 높은 안전성을 보장해요 ←정답

❌ ③ 스캔 비교로 일치를 찾는 점 — 훨씬 앞의 과정이라 This가 직접 가리키는 대상이 아니에요.

❌ ④ 손만으로 물건을 사는 점 — 편의에 관한 내용이지 안전성의 근거가 아니에요.
det.tip: This = 앞 문장 '정맥 패턴이 고유·본인 모르게 채취 불가'라는 점

ch: 손바닥 스캔이 신용카드와 현금을 대체한다는 사실
정맥 패턴이 고유하며 본인 모르게 쉽게 채취될 수 없다는 점
스캔이 완료되면 기존 스캔과 비교되어 일치를 찾는다는 점
사람들이 손만으로 물건을 살 수 있게 된다는 점

questions.passage: It is now believed that deserts may be perfect places for ①<u>harvesting</u> solar power. If this is true, there would be no other place as ideal as the Sahara, the world's largest desert. Unfortunately, solar farms in the desert could have adverse environmental effects. For example, ②<u>covering</u> half the Sahara with solar farms would raise local temperatures by approximately 2.5 °C. This warming would not be limited to the desert — it would spread around the globe, eventually increasing the world's average temperature by 0.39 °C. This could speed up global warming by ③<u>melted</u> sea ice and exposing the dark water beneath it, which absorbs greater amounts of solar energy than sea ice does. Rising temperatures in the Sahara could also cause other problems by ④<u>changing</u> global precipitation patterns, including droughts in the Amazon and more frequent tropical cyclones.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: melted → melting (전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사가 오므로 melting)
det.analysis:
① harvesting: 'for harvesting solar power' 전치사 for 뒤 동명사 — 적절해요.

② covering: 'covering half the Sahara ~ would raise' 문장의 주어 역할을 하는 동명사 — 적절해요.

③ melted: 'This could speed up global warming by ___ sea ice ~'에서 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 해요. 뒤의 and exposing과도 나란히 이어지므로 과거분사 melted가 아니라 melting이 맞아요 ←정답

④ changing: 'by changing global precipitation patterns' 전치사 by 뒤 동명사 — 적절해요.
det.tip: by + 동명사(~함으로써). by melting sea ice and exposing ~ (병렬)

questions.passage: Research suggests that when we use the term "brilliant," we usually apply it to men rather than women. It is said that this is an unconscious bias that occurs all across the world. It may also be the reason why even brilliant women are less likely to be employed in fields where a high level of intelligence is prized, such as math and science. A study conducted in 2016 analyzed 14 million student reviews of university faculty members. It found that male professors were two to three times more likely to be described with the words "brilliant" or "genius" than female professors were. Furthermore, students were more likely to use these words in reference to professors of physics and philosophy, two fields with relatively few women. These results suggest that we either underestimate women or overestimate men. This is why we need to be aware of the words we use and think about why we use them.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ① 원문 S1 'apply it to men rather than women'을 바꿔 말함 → 일치
det.analysis:
① 여성보다 남성에게 더 자주 부여함 = 'we usually apply it to men rather than women'을 바꿔 말함 ←정답(일치)
② 겨우 수천 건? 본문은 '1,400만 건(14 million)'을 분석함 — 불일치
③ 여성 비율이 높음? 본문은 물리·철학이 여성이 '적은(few)' 분야라고 함 — 불일치
④ 최근 특정 국가에서? 본문은 '전 세계적으로(all across the world)' 일어난다고 함 — 불일치
det.tip: apply it to men rather than women = 남성에게 더 자주 부여(일치)

ch: 사람들은 '뛰어난(brilliant)'이라는 칭찬을 여성보다 남성에게 더 자주 부여하는 경향이 있다.
2016년 연구는 겨우 수천 건의 강의 후기만을 분석 대상으로 삼았다.
물리학과 철학은 여성 비율이 유난히 높은 분야로 나타났다.
이러한 편견은 최근에야 특정 국가에서 처음 생겨난 현상이다.

questions.passage: One team of researchers has devised an unusual plan to deal with this. They intend to record the sounds of healthy reefs and then play them near reefs that are __________ (suffer) from severe bleaching.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.korean: suffer(동사: 시달리다) → suffering(현재분사): 'be동사 + 현재분사' 진행형
det.analysis:
빈칸이 든 부분은 'reefs that are ___ (suffer) from severe bleaching'예요.

① 괄호 안 suffer는 '(고통·피해에) 시달리다'라는 동사예요. 바로 앞에 be동사 are가 있어요.

② 'be동사 + 현재분사'는 '~하고 있는 중이다'라는 진행형이에요. 관계사절의 주어 reefs가 심한 백화에 '시달리고 있는' 중이므로, 동사 suffer를 현재분사 suffering으로 바꿔 'are suffering from(~에 시달리고 있다)'으로 써야 해요.
det.tip: be동사(are) + 현재분사 → are suffering (진행형)

questions.passage: Local elementary schools are invited to join us in celebrating the 25th anniversary of the city's subway system. We're asking elementary students to create a poster that will be displayed in our subways during the celebration. The theme of the poster should be "uniting communities." Be creative and show us what the subway means to you and your community. Each student may submit only one poster by September 22. This event is less about competition than it is about showcasing community spirit. However, the winner will receive a special subway tour, and the winner's school will receive $500. __________ and all of the winner's classmates. The judging period will take no longer than one week. So we expect to announce a winner by October 1. We hope everyone participates!
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 빈칸을 완성하시오. (10단어) (영어로)
'우승자를 포함하는 홍보용 사진 촬영도 있을 것이다'
[조건] (1) There, a, also, be, featuring, photoshoot, promotional, the, will, winner를 모두 사용
(2) 10단어로 쓸 것
(3) There will be 구문으로 시작할 것

det.korean: There will also be a promotional photoshoot featuring the winner = 우승자를 포함하는 홍보용 사진 촬영도 있을 것이다
det.analysis:
'~도 있을 것이다'는 「There will (also) be ~」 구문으로 나타내요. There will be 뒤에 존재하는 대상 'a promotional photoshoot(홍보용 사진 촬영)'을 놓아요.

그 명사구를 뒤에서 꾸미는 현재분사 featuring(~을 포함하는)을 붙이고, 목적어로 the winner(우승자)를 놓아요.

순서: There + will + also + be + a + promotional + photoshoot + featuring + the + winner.
det.tip: There will (also) be + 명사(있을 것이다) + 현재분사(featuring)로 후치수식

questions.wa: There will also be a promotional photoshoot featuring the winner
accept: There will also be a promotional photoshoot featuring the winner

questions.passage: This is __________ (call) the "downdraught effect." Generally, the higher you go, the stronger the winds are. When strong winds high above the ground hit a tall building, they can't go through it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: call(동사: 부르다) → called. 「be동사 + 과거분사(p.p.)」의 수동태로 '~라고 불리다'라는 뜻
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장은 'This is ______ (call) the "downdraught effect."(이것은 하강 기류 효과라고 ______)'예요. 주어 This 뒤에 be동사 is가 있고, '~라고 불리다'라는 뜻이 되어야 하므로 「be동사 + 과거분사(p.p.)」의 수동태가 필요해요. 따라서 동사원형 call을 과거분사 called로 바꿔 is called(~라고 불리다)로 써야 해요.

call(X, 능동 원형) → called(O, be동사 is 뒤에 오는 수동태 과거분사)
det.tip: be동사(is) + 과거분사(called) = 수동태 '~라고 불리다'. call → called

questions.passage: Hoarding disorder is a mental illness characterized by the inability to get rid of possessions that have no use or value. It is often accompanied by "excessive acquisition," which means sufferers feel the need to own as many things as possible. Hoarding behavior tends to start at an early age and becomes more and more extreme as the person grows older. Once it becomes a significant problem, __________, which helps hoarders make better decisions about keeping or getting rid of their belongings. However, as hoarding disorder can be a complex condition with multiple causes, this treatment often takes a long time, and additional methods may be required.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 빈칸을 완성하시오. (7단어) (영어로)
'그것은 대개 행동 치료로 치료된다'
[조건] (1) behavioral, generally, is, it, therapy, treated, with를 모두 사용
(2) 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: it is generally treated with behavioral therapy = 그것은 대개 행동 치료로 치료된다
det.analysis:
주어 it(그것은=저장 강박)으로 시작해요.

'치료된다'는 '치료받는' 대상이므로 수동태 be동사 + 과거분사로 써요: is treated(치료된다). '대개'라는 부사 generally는 be동사와 과거분사 사이에 넣어요(is generally treated).

'행동 치료로'는 수단을 나타내는 전치사 with를 써서 with behavioral therapy로 붙여요.

순서: it + is + generally + treated + with + behavioral therapy.
det.tip: 수동태 be + 과거분사(is treated) / 부사는 be동사 뒤 / with = ~로(수단)

questions.wa: it is generally treated with behavioral therapy
accept: it is generally treated with behavioral therapy

questions.passage: They may look pretty, but consider this — perfectly fine produce that looks a little different is being wasted. In fact, some farmers end up __________ (throw) away as much as 50 percent of their harvest because it doesn't look quite right. Fortunately, this is beginning to change.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: throw(동사: 던지다, 버리다) → throwing. 'end up + -ing(결국 ~하게 되다)'의 동명사 형태
det.analysis: 동사 throw를 동명사 throwing으로 바꿔야 해요. 'end up + -ing'는 '결국 ~하게 되다'라는 뜻의 표현이라, end up 뒤에는 반드시 동명사(-ing)가 와요. 그래서 throw away(버리다)를 throwing away로 바꿔 'end up throwing away(결국 버리게 되다)'가 돼요. 동사원형 throw는 end up 뒤에 올 수 없어요.
det.tip: end up + 동명사(-ing) = 결국 ~하게 되다 → end up throwing away
